# Darkroom Printing

## Overview

I use resin-coated paper in 8x10 trays, one each for developer, stop, fixer and wash. The safelight is a dim orange bulb, positioned well away from the trays so it does not fog the sheets during a long session. I run an extractor fan because the chemistry fumes build up in a closed room, and I keep a window cracked even in winter. Resin-coated stock washes and dries faster than fibre, which suits the small space I have. A cheap enlarger with a 50 mm lens does everything I need for 35 mm negatives. The room doubles as a laundry, so everything packs down into a cupboard when I am done. I mix chemistry from liquid concentrates and store it in clearly labelled bottles under the sink, away from the trays. Negatives live in a binder ordered by date, so finding a frame again is quick.

## Steps

Stop the enlarger lens down to f/8, then make a test strip in 2-second increments across the sheet to find a base exposure. Developer runs at 20 C for 90 seconds with gentle agitation. Stop bath is 30 seconds, then fixer for 5 minutes. Wash for 10 minutes in running water, then squeegee the surface and hang the sheet to dry. I set the timer before each stage and keep the trays in a fixed order so I never reach for the wrong one. Temperature matters more than anything else; I check it with a thermometer before starting.

## Troubleshooting

Muddy blacks usually mean the developer is exhausted or too cold; I check the temperature and mix fresh from stock. Dust specks come from a dirty negative or a grubby drying area, so I use a blower bulb and lint-free cloths on the glass. Uneven development shows as blotchy patches and traces to lazy agitation; I rock the tray on a steady rhythm and do not walk away. Flat, grey results point at expired paper or a weak dilution. A thin white line down the edge is a scratched negative, so I check the holder before the next exposure. If the result is too dense overall, I stop the lens down one more stop or shorten each exposure step, rather than fiddling with the developer.
